related_questions.question: What are the long term effects of COVID-19?

text_blocks.snippet: Many individuals who have had COVID-19, even those with mild initial symptoms, can experience long-term effects, often referred to as long COVID or post-COVID-19 condition. These effects can manifest as a range of persistent symptoms that can last for weeks, months, or even longer.

list.title: Extreme tiredness (fatigue):
list.snippet: This can be debilitating, and often worsens after physical or mental activity.

list.title: Cognitive difficulties (brain fog):
list.snippet: Problems with memory, concentration, and thinking clearly are frequently reported.

list.title: Shortness of breath:
list.snippet: Difficulty breathing or feeling winded can persist for a considerable time.

list.title: Other symptoms:
list.snippet: These can include headaches, sleep disturbances, dizziness, loss of taste or smell, and gastrointestinal issues, according to the Mayo Clinic.

list.title: New or worsening illnesses:
list.snippet: Some individuals develop or experience worsening of conditions like heart disease, mood disorders (anxiety, depression), autoimmune diseases, and chronic fatigue syndrome.
While anyone can develop long COVID, certain individuals may be more susceptible. The World Health Organization states that the condition can occur even after mild or asymptomatic initial infections.
Some research suggests that individuals with certain pre-existing conditions, like diabetes or obesity, may be at higher risk.
Long COVID can significantly impact daily life, affecting work, school, and social activities.
While some symptoms may resolve over time, others can persist or fluctuate.
Research is ongoing to better understand the long-term effects of COVID-19 and develop effective treatments.

related_questions.question: What damage can COVID do to your body?
related_questions.snippet: By some estimates, 400 million people worldwide have been diagnosed with some form of long Covid. But an infection can also lead to other issues, including lung and heart damage and microbiome changes in the gut, that may not always be recognized as long Covid but can still have a lasting effect on our health.

related_questions.question: How long does it take to recover from COVID?
related_questions.snippet: Early research suggested that it could take two weeks for your body to get over a mild illness or up to six weeks for severe or critical cases. Recovery varies for different people, depending on things like your age and overall health. Fatigue, headache, and troubled breathing are the symptoms most likely to linger.

related_questions.question: What's the quickest way to get rid of COVID symptoms?

text_blocks.snippet: The fastest way to recover from COVID-19 symptoms depends on the severity of the illness. For mild cases, rest, hydration, and over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen or ibuprofen can help manage symptoms. For those at higher risk, early treatment with medications like Paxlovid is crucial and must be started within 5-7 days of symptom onset to be effective, according to the CDC.

list.title: Hydration:
list.snippet: Staying hydrated by drinking plenty of fluids is important.

list.title: Monitor symptoms:
list.snippet: Keep an eye on your symptoms and contact a doctor if they worsen or if you experience any emergency warning signs, says UnityPoint Health.
